findings.description: The try/except at evox_runner.py:2799 catches only OSError. If ctypes.CDLL('libc.so.6') succeeds but the loaded library does not export malloc_trim (theoretically possible on a glibc variant or if libc.so.6 is a stub), an AttributeError would propagate uncaught. In practice, any system with libc.so.6 is glibc and exports malloc_trim, so the risk is negligible — but for completeness, the except clause should cover both OSError and AttributeError.
findings.fix: Change `except OSError:` to `except (OSError, AttributeError):` on line 2803 of evox_runner.py. This is a one-word change that costs nothing and future-proofs against exotic libc variants.

code_quality_notes: All three changes are clean, well-scoped, and correctly documented. The docstring updates at config.py:407-411 (cache) and config.py:1102-1107 (epoch gens) provide clear rationale with historical context. The malloc_trim addition at evox_runner.py:2793+ is properly guarded with a try/except for portability. Import of ctypes inside the block is safe — Python caches module imports, so the repeated `import ctypes` every 3 gens is a cheap sys.modules dict lookup, not a filesystem hit. The libc.so.6 CDLL approach is the standard Linux idiom for calling glibc's malloc_trim and poses no security risk (it loads the already-loaded standard C library). No stale references to old values remain in production code.
test_adequacy_notes: The test update in test_config_additions.py (==25 → ==13) is correct and necessary. The test_epoch_rounds_cover_budget test in test_phase2_island_scheduler.py dynamically reads the config constant, so it auto-adapts to the new value and passed. There is no dedicated unit test for the malloc_trim path, but writing one would require mocking ctypes.CDLL (or running on Linux), and the try/except guard makes it a safe no-op on all platforms. A test for this defensive code path would have low ROI given the simplicity of the addition. The existing test suites (218 tests, all green) provide adequate regression coverage for the behavioral boundaries affected by these config changes.
recommendations: Consider broadening the except clause from OSError to (OSError, AttributeError) for maximum portability — one additional exception type costs nothing.

Optional: move `import ctypes` to the top of evox_runner.py as a top-level import. The current inline import is functionally correct (sys.modules cache) but unconventional. This is purely a style preference, not a defect.
